text: The 15 cm sIG 33 (schweres Infanterie Geschuetz 33) was the standard German heavy infantry gun used in the Second World War. It was the largest weapon ever classified as an infantry gun by any nation.<cr>Sources differ on the development history, but the gun itself was of conventional design. Early production models were horse-drawn, with wooden wheels. Later production models had pressed steel wheels, with solid rubber tires and air brakes for motor towing.<cr>The sIG 33 was rather heavy for its mission and it was redesigned in the late 1930s to incorporate light alloys in an effort to save weight. This saved about 150 kilograms (330 lb), but the outbreak of war forced the return to the original design before more than a few hundred were made, as the Luftwaffe had a higher priority for light alloys. A new carriage, made entirely of light alloys, was tested around 1939, but was not accepted for service.<cr><cr>
translation: 15厘米重型步兵炮sIG 33（schweres Infanterie Geschütz 33）是德国在第二次世界大战中使用的标准重型步兵火炮。它是任何国家分类为步兵炮的最大武器。<cr>资料来源对开发历史存在分歧，但该火炮本身设计传统。早期生产型号使用马匹牵引，并配有木轮。后期生产型号则配备了压铸钢轮、实心橡胶轮胎和用于机动牵引的空气制动器。<cr>sIG 33对于其任务来说相对较重，在20世纪30年代晚期进行了重新设计，以采用轻合金来减轻重量。这大约节省了150公斤（330磅），但战争爆发迫使恢复到原始设计，因为空军对轻合金有更高的优先权。<cr>一种全新的全部由轻合金制成的炮架在约1939年进行测试，但未被接受服役。
